references.text: The same principle of burning what remains of the Passover lamb with fire before morning, to ensure that holy food is not profaned.
At the consecration of the priests at Sinai, the same command was given to burn what remained of the consecrated meat and bread with fire.
Law regarding the thank offering: what remains on the third day must be burned with fire, illustrating the general principle for handling sacrificial leftovers.
Earlier in the same chapter, the ox as a sin offering is burned with fire outside the camp, demonstrating the use of fire in sacrificial rituals.
Rule concerning the peace offering: what remains on the third day must be burned with fire, confirming the practice of burning sacrificial leftovers.
